thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Spike in 5xxs from eu-north-1/az-n across multiple services. Initial anomaly detected at 2026-03-15T03:20:00Z. Affected path: NAT gateway egress -> external dependency timeouts. Paging maya (on-call).

maya: I got it, jumping in. Are we seeing route flaps or conntrack exhaustion?

raj: quick summary — hit 30% 5xx rate on prod frontends, origin logs show upstream connection resets when egress goes via az-n nat-gw-03. Other AZs look ok.

samantha: seeing NAT errors + repeated target unreachable in VPC flow logs. Packet drops around 03:17-03:21.

cam: possible route-table drift after a recent infra change windows back. Can someone check route table associations for subnet private-*-azn?

maya: assigning tasks — @raj check NAT health and metrics, @cam check route associations and any recent terraform applies, @maria triage customer-facing impact.

raj: checking NAT console now. nat-gw-03 shows healthy checks but connection failures spike on metrics. QPS normal. conntrack entries trending up.

raj: runbook step: rotating NAT (failover to nat-gw-01) to confirm impact mitigation. Executing now — will reassign route on the private subnet to nat-gw-01.

deploy-bot: NOTE: automated safety lock — cannot modify route-assoc during active deploy windows without approval. Override requested by maya.

maya: override acked, proceeding.

cam: while that's happening, I'm running `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-priv-azn` to confirm. Output shows two associated tables, one unexpected (rtb-drift-legacy).

samantha: hmm rtbs with overlapping 0.0.0.0/0 targets -> one to nat-gw-03, another to local IGW? Could cause asymmetric return paths.

maya: confirm: a legacy route-table got associated with two subnets during a manual fix earlier. We'll detach rtb-drift-legacy from subnet-priv-azn and re-assoc rtb-standard-priv. Cam, do the detach and assoc.

cam: doing detach+associate now. Command: ```
aws ec2 disassociate-route-table --association-id rtbassoc-0abc1234
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id rtb-0f9e8d7c --subnet-id subnet-priv-azn
```

cam: assoc complete. Confirming 0.0.0.0/0 now points to nat-gw-01.

raj: NAT failover in effect. I'm watching conntrack: entries dropping back to baseline. Backend 5xxs decreasing.

maria: support note — noticed a cluster of customer API errors ~03:18-03:22 from EU region. Impact: elevated error rates for ~4-6% of requests for ~5 minutes. Opening interim incident status page.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03015-azn-nat-route-drift. Severity: Sev2. Pages forwarded to SRE rotation.

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged by maya (on-call). On-call handoff scheduled if needed.

maya: brief post-mit checklist — keep NAT pinned to nat-gw-01 for now, block any terraform runs on route tables in eu-north-1, collect diffs and audit who/what associated rtb-drift-legacy.

samantha: collecting VPC event history: CloudTrail shows `AssociateRouteTable` by `infra-ops@redwood` from IP 52.13.24.10 at 2026-03-15T02:58Z. There was an automated remediation job that touched subnets.

cam: we should roll forward a fix rather than just revert: create a policy to prevent multiple route-tables with overlapping 0.0.0.0/0 associations in the same AZ. I'll open a PR after we stabilize.

raj: for near-term stabilization I also rotated NAT elastic IP (EIP swap) on nat-gw-03 to clear conntrack sticky translations. That was done at 03:28. No further spikes after assoc.

maria: composing customer notification draft: short summary, impacted region eu-north-1, window 03:17-03:23 UTC, intermittent 5xxs, root cause route-table drift causing asymmetric egress -> NAT failover mitigated. Sending to legal/comms for approval.

maya: timeline so far: 03:17 detect, 03:20 page, 03:22 identify rtb drift, 03:24 reassociate route-table, 03:28 NAT EIP rotate, 03:30 metrics normal.

samantha: capturing logs/snippets: VPC flow log sample showing `REJECT`/`UNREACHABLE` during window and then `ACCEPT` post-fix. I'll attach to the incident.

cam: temporary mitigations: 1) block route-table changes via sentinel policy, 2) put route-table assoc guard in CI, 3) schedule cleanup of legacy rtb objects.

raj: adding NAT metrics panel to the incident dashboard for long-term watch — include conntrack, active ports, failure_count.

maya: green check, will keep monitoring for 2h. If stable, we'll drop to Sev3 and schedule a postmortem.

maria: tagging customers who reported with the draft and ETA for follow-up after PM.

incident-bot: Update logged to INC-2026-03015-azn-nat-route-drift. Links: https://rc.infra/incidents/INC-2026-03015-azn-nat-route-drift (internal).

maya: thanks team. Quick note for the postmortem — include the infra automation runbook and a policy gap that allowed legacy rtb re-assoc. Also add a step to validate route table uniqueness for egress.

samantha: will own the postmortem doc.

cam: PR will include a terraform lock plus sentinel check.

maria: will coordinate customer comms after approvals.

maya: closing active mitigation. Keeping channel open for any regressions. :thumbsup:
